- **Dispatch ≠ success** — handing an event to the publish pipeline is not the same as it landing. Rust owns a **local publish intent / status fact** (pending → signed → stored → planned → sent → failed/exhausted), so the app gets honest, offline-first write state instead of optimistic fire-and-forget.
 [...] **4. A local publish intent is created immediately — before anything touches the network.**
The first thing the kernel does is mint a **status fact** owned by Rust: `pending`. This is the offline-first root — the write exists and is durable *before* a signer or relay is involved. This is why "dispatch ≠ success": the app gets a real status object, not a fire-and-forget. [...] 
**8. Status streams back out the read door — reactively, no polling.**
As relay `OK`/`AUTH`/error responses arrive, the kernel advances the status fact to terminal states (`sent`, `failed`, `exhausted`) and pushes those out as `ViewBatch` snapshots. The shell *observes* the write's status the same way it observes any read — via pushed snapshots, never by polling. So the UI shows "sending… / published / failed" off real Rust-owned state.
